pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: src/features/inflight/live/LiveWarRoomHeader.test.ts:27 The deadline-countdown suite asserts a private copy of daysUntil kept inside the test file, while the production helper it claims to pin is now exported (LiveWarRoomGoalBanner.tsx:32) and no test imports it, so a regression in the shipped helper leaves every assertion green.

techniques.evidence: src/features/inflight/live/LiveWarRoomHeader.test.ts:27 The test drives a copy of the helper, not the production decision. Its header comment (lines 6-7) says the helper is module-private with no exported seam, but production now exports it, so the lift-into-a-reachable-unit repair is already available and unused. No dom test in the folder asserts the countdown either (grep for deadline/daysUntil across *.dom.test.tsx finds nothing).

src/features/inflight/live/LiveWarRoomGoalBanner.tsx:32 Mutating this production function cannot turn the suite red, because the only test of it never imports it. The instrument cannot fail on the protection it names.

pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: src/lib/llm/bedrock.test.ts:18 Provider suites swap the vendor SDK class for hand-built response shapes, so the seam sits above the client library's serialization layer and nothing would notice an upstream change. The only real-provider lane (llm-bench, LLM_BENCH=1) is opt-in, manual and kept out of CI.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/llm/bedrock.test.ts:18 This is a hand-written fake of the SDK class, not a recording at the wire. The Gemini fake in provider.test.ts:18-28 is likewise modelled on what the consumer reads. The freshness obligation is met only by src/lib/llm/bench/llm-bench.test.ts:31, which is opt-in (LLM_BENCH === "1") and documented as never run in CI, so it is not a scheduled certification lane.
src/lib/llm/bedrock.test.ts:81 The per-call timeout cutoff is proved on a fake clock against a send() that rejects only when its abort signal fires. No wall-clock bound is involved.

src/lib/llm/index.test.ts:28 Every provider-availability env var is stubbed empty, so the host machine's real AWS, Gemini and Nebius config cannot leak into the selection assertions. What the test inherits is declared.

pairs.registryProposal: recorded-interaction-fixtures could say how its 'trivial enough to fake honestly' exemption applies to LLM SDKs: a text-plus-usage response looks trivial, but the tool-use and thinking-budget shapes are not, and the technique gives no threshold.
